frontmatter.title: Myth Busting
frontmatter.adaptation_notes:
Game-specific myths: Some reference US casino culture.
Humor: One-liners use irreverent tone. Adapt for profile.
Format: Social card copy may need cultural adjustment.

myths.title: The Hot Streak

socialCard.myth: I'm on a hot streak — keep going!
socialCard.fact: Independent spins do not carry a winning streak forward. The same rules and settings apply to the next spin.
socialCard.stat: The previous wins do not change its odds

myths.articleExplainer:
Four wins aren't a forecast.

Independent spins do not carry a winning streak forward. The same rules and settings apply to the next spin.

quiz.question: On a slot with independent spins, you win four times. With the same game settings, what changes on spin five?

options.label: Better than normal — you're on a streak
Worse than normal — you're "due" for a loss
The previous wins do not change its odds
Depends on how much you bet

quiz.feedback: Independent spins do not carry a winning streak forward. The same rules and settings apply to the next spin.

myths.title: Due for a Win

socialCard.myth: This machine hasn't paid out in ages — it's due.
socialCard.fact: A losing run does not make an independent spin due. Check any separate bonus features in the game rules.

myths.articleExplainer:
A losing run isn't a countdown.

A losing run does not make an independent spin due. Check any separate bonus features in the game rules.

quiz.question: On a slot with independent spins, three hours pass without a win. What does that predict about the next spin?

options.label: It's more likely to pay out soon
It's less likely to pay out — it's "cold"

quiz.feedback: A losing run does not make an independent spin due. Check any separate bonus features in the game rules.

myths.title: The Lucky Machine

socialCard.fact: Memorable wins can shape an impression. A complete record includes stakes and losses. Different games and settings can have different odds.
socialCard.stat: Compare the complete record, including losses

myths.articleExplainer:
Favourite seat. Check the facts.

Memorable wins can shape an impression. A complete record includes stakes and losses. Different games and settings can have different odds.

quiz.question: A slot feels lucky because you remember its wins. What would help you check that impression?

options.label: Compare the complete record, including losses

quiz.feedback: Memorable wins can shape an impression. A complete record includes stakes and losses. Different games and settings can have different odds.

myths.title: Near Misses Mean You're Close

socialCard.myth: Two cherries and a blank — I almost hit it! One more try.
socialCard.fact: A near miss is still a non-winning result under that game's paytable. It does not make an independent next spin more likely to win.
socialCard.stat: No — the near miss does not improve them

myths.articleExplainer:
Close isn't a countdown.

A near miss is still a non-winning result under that game's paytable. It does not make an independent next spin more likely to win.

quiz.question: A non-winning result looks close on a slot with independent spins. Does that improve the next spin's odds?

options.label: You're getting closer to a win
No — the near miss does not improve them

quiz.feedback: A near miss is still a non-winning result under that game's paytable. It does not make an independent next spin more likely to win.

myths.title: Time of Day Matters

socialCard.myth: Slots pay out more at night / weekends / when the casino is full.
socialCard.fact: Time of day alone is not evidence of a higher RTP. Read the game's rules and published return information; requirements vary by market.
socialCard.stat: No — check the game's published information

myths.articleExplainer:
The clock isn't a paytable.

Time of day alone is not evidence of a higher RTP. Read the game's rules and published return information; requirements vary by market.

quiz.question: Can the clock alone tell you a slot game's return-to-player percentage?

options.label: No — check the game's published information

quiz.feedback: Time of day alone is not evidence of a higher RTP. Read the game's rules and published return information; requirements vary by market.

myths.title: Higher Bets Improve Your Odds

socialCard.fact: The percentage is unchanged in this example. A ten-times larger stake has ten-times larger expected loss. Other games may change payouts with the stake.

myths.articleExplainer:
A bigger stake changes the amount at risk.

The percentage is unchanged in this example. A ten-times larger stake has ten-times larger expected loss. Other games may change payouts with the stake.

quiz.question: On the same roulette bet, with the same rules and payout ratio, what happens to the house-edge percentage if your stake rises?

options.label: It goes down — casinos reward bigger bettors
It goes up — the casino takes more

quiz.feedback: The percentage is unchanged in this example. A ten-times larger stake has ten-times larger expected loss. Other games may change payouts with the stake.

myths.title: Betting Systems Beat the House

socialCard.myth: Just use the Martingale system — double your bet after every loss. You'll always come out ahead.
socialCard.fact: A betting sequence does not change roulette's probabilities or payout ratio. Repeated losses require larger stakes, and funds or table limits can stop the sequence.
socialCard.stat: No — and the required stakes can grow quickly

myths.articleExplainer:
A sequence isn't an advantage.

A betting sequence does not change roulette's probabilities or payout ratio. Repeated losses require larger stakes, and funds or table limits can stop the sequence.

quiz.question: Does doubling your roulette stake after every loss remove the house edge?

options.label: No — and the required stakes can grow quickly
Yes — there is no limit to the required stake

quiz.feedback: A betting sequence does not change roulette's probabilities or payout ratio. Repeated losses require larger stakes, and funds or table limits can stop the sequence.

myths.title: The Dealer Is Hot or Cold

socialCard.myth: Switch tables — that dealer is too hot.
socialCard.fact: A streak alone does not establish an advantage. Blackjack rules, strategy and the cards remaining can matter; hands dealt from a shoe are not independent.
socialCard.stat: No — compare the rules and game conditions

myths.articleExplainer:
Check the rules, not the run.

A streak alone does not establish an advantage. Blackjack rules, strategy and the cards remaining can matter; hands dealt from a shoe are not independent.

quiz.question: Does a dealer's recent winning streak alone tell you which blackjack table has better odds?

options.label: No — compare the rules and game conditions

quiz.feedback: A streak alone does not establish an advantage. Blackjack rules, strategy and the cards remaining can matter; hands dealt from a shoe are not independent.

myths.title: Card Counting Is Easy Money

socialCard.myth: I saw it in a movie — just count cards and beat the house.
socialCard.fact: Any potential advantage depends on the rules, shoe composition and play. Results vary, including losing periods, and venues may restrict play.

myths.articleExplainer:
An advantage isn't a guarantee.

Any potential advantage depends on the rules, shoe composition and play. Results vary, including losing periods, and venues may restrict play.

quiz.question: Does card counting guarantee income from blackjack?
quiz.feedback: Any potential advantage depends on the rules, shoe composition and play. Results vary, including losing periods, and venues may restrict play.

myths.title: Choosing "Your" Numbers Improves Odds

socialCard.myth: I always play 17 — it's my lucky number.
socialCard.fact: There are 37 equally likely pockets in this example. Previous results do not change the next independent spin's probability.

myths.articleExplainer:
Your number. The same odds.

There are 37 equally likely pockets in this example. Previous results do not change the next independent spin's probability.

quiz.question: On a fair single-zero roulette wheel, number 7 has missed 50 spins. What is its chance on the next independent spin?

options.label: It depends on where the dealer drops the ball

quiz.feedback: There are 37 equally likely pockets in this example. Previous results do not change the next independent spin's probability.

myths.title: Knowing the Sport Means You'll Win

socialCard.myth: I know football better than anyone — of course I'll make money betting on it.
socialCard.fact: Risking $110 wins $100 profit. Break-even is 110 ÷ (110 + 100), or about 52.4%. This assumes equal stakes, the same price and no pushes or extra fees.

myths.articleExplainer:
Knowing the sport starts the conversation.

Risking $110 wins $100 profit. Break-even is 110 ÷ (110 + 100), or about 52.4%. This assumes equal stakes, the same price and no pushes or extra fees.

quiz.question: With equal stakes at −110, no pushes and no extra fees, what win rate breaks even?
quiz.feedback: Risking $110 wins $100 profit. Break-even is 110 ÷ (110 + 100), or about 52.4%. This assumes equal stakes, the same price and no pushes or extra fees.

myths.title: Parlays Are a Smart Strategy

socialCard.myth: A bigger parlay payout means a better chance.
socialCard.fact: 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.0625. This example assumes independence; correlated picks need different calculations. A quoted payout is a separate figure.

myths.articleExplainer:
Four picks. One all-win result.

0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.0625. This example assumes independence; correlated picks need different calculations. A quoted payout is a separate figure.

quiz.question: Four independent picks each have a true 50% chance. What is the chance all four win?
quiz.feedback: 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.0625. This example assumes independence; correlated picks need different calculations. A quoted payout is a separate figure.

myths.title: Following Tipsters Guarantees Profit

socialCard.myth: Eight wins from ten picks proves a tipster will make a profit.
socialCard.fact: Ten picks are a limited sample. To assess a claim, check the complete record, prices, stakes, losses and fees. Accuracy alone is not profit.
socialCard.stat: It does not establish a reliable long-term profit

myths.articleExplainer:
A highlight reel isn't a balance sheet.

Ten picks are a limited sample. To assess a claim, check the complete record, prices, stakes, losses and fees. Accuracy alone is not profit.

quiz.question: A tipster reports eight wins from ten picks. What can that record alone establish?

options.label: It does not establish a reliable long-term profit

quiz.feedback: Ten picks are a limited sample. To assess a claim, check the complete record, prices, stakes, losses and fees. Accuracy alone is not profit.

myths.title: In-Play Betting Gives You an Edge

socialCard.myth: I can see how the game is going — live betting lets me react and win.
socialCard.fact: Live prices can change, and broadcasts can be delayed. Review the accepted price, stake and potential return. Watching the match does not guarantee an information advantage.
socialCard.stat: The current price and potential return

myths.articleExplainer:
The score moves. The price can too.

Live prices can change, and broadcasts can be delayed. Review the accepted price, stake and potential return. Watching the match does not guarantee an information advantage.

quiz.question: Before accepting a live bet after the price changes, which detail matters?

options.label: The current price and potential return
The size of your last win

quiz.feedback: Live prices can change, and broadcasts can be delayed. Review the accepted price, stake and potential return. Watching the match does not guarantee an information advantage.

myths.title: Some Numbers Are "Due"

socialCard.myth: Number 23 hasn't been drawn in months — it's overdue.
socialCard.fact: A fair independent draw does not compensate for previous results. In a fair six-from-49 draw, each six-number combination has a 1-in-13,983,816 chance.
socialCard.stat: No — its past absence does not improve its chance

myths.articleExplainer:
Missing isn't overdue.

A fair independent draw does not compensate for previous results. In a fair six-from-49 draw, each six-number combination has a 1-in-13,983,816 chance.

quiz.question: In a fair lottery with independent draws, a number has not appeared for six months. Is it more likely next time?

options.label: Yes — the law of averages says it must come up eventually
No — its past absence does not improve its chance
It depends on how many total numbers are in the draw

quiz.feedback: A fair independent draw does not compensate for previous results. In a fair six-from-49 draw, each six-number combination has a 1-in-13,983,816 chance.

myths.title: Buying More Tickets Dramatically Improves Odds

socialCard.myth: Buying 100 lottery tickets makes the jackpot likely.
socialCard.fact: The chance is 100 times that of one combination, and the cost is 100 times as much at a fixed price. Duplicate combinations do not add distinct ways to win the jackpot.

myths.articleExplainer:
More combinations. More cost.

The chance is 100 times that of one combination, and the cost is 100 times as much at a fixed price. Duplicate combinations do not add distinct ways to win the jackpot.

quiz.question: In one fair six-from-49 draw, what jackpot chance do 100 distinct combinations give?
quiz.feedback: The chance is 100 times that of one combination, and the cost is 100 times as much at a fixed price. Duplicate combinations do not add distinct ways to win the jackpot.

myths.title: You Can Win Back Your Losses

socialCard.myth: If I keep playing, the game has to pay me back.
socialCard.fact: An earlier loss does not create a repayment obligation. Additional play at negative expected value adds expected loss, although any session can vary. A budget can help you decide when to stop.
socialCard.stat: No — further bets put more money at risk

myths.articleExplainer:
A budget is a limit, not a target.

An earlier loss does not create a repayment obligation. Additional play at negative expected value adds expected loss, although any session can vary. A budget can help you decide when to stop.

quiz.question: On a game with a house edge, does an earlier loss make recovering that money certain?

options.label: Yes — eventually it must repay you
No — further bets put more money at risk
Yes — a larger stake guarantees it

quiz.feedback: An earlier loss does not create a repayment obligation. Additional play at negative expected value adds expected loss, although any session can vary. A budget can help you decide when to stop.

myths.title: Gambling Is a Way to Make Money

socialCard.myth: A house edge guarantees a specific result in my session.
socialCard.fact: A positive house edge describes the game's long-run mathematical cost under specified rules. It does not predict a particular session. Treat gambling as entertainment with a budget.
socialCard.stat: An expected return below the amount wagered

myths.articleExplainer:
Know the cost of the entertainment.

A positive house edge describes the game's long-run mathematical cost under specified rules. It does not predict a particular session. Treat gambling as entertainment with a budget.

quiz.question: What does a positive house edge describe?

options.label: A fee charged after every win
An expected return below the amount wagered

quiz.feedback: A positive house edge describes the game's long-run mathematical cost under specified rules. It does not predict a particular session. Treat gambling as entertainment with a budget.
